questions.question: Was replacing the MCP server (ai_mem/server.py, mem_* tools) with a CLI/scripts, or packaging ai-mem as a Claude Code plugin, ever considered, tried or rejected? Why?

runs.answer:
Yes, it was decided and is in progress, not just considered. On 2026-10-10 the decision was to drop the MCP server (server.py, mem_* tools) and package ai-mem as a Claude Code plugin without .mcp.json. The plugin would contain a stdlib-only CLI for writes (format and path validation), reads through Read/Glob/Grep and the librarian agent, agents/skills/SessionStart hook as plugin parts, and a setup assistant that wires the framework into the user's workflows.

Why (as recorded): the value had shifted from the tool to the practice (records in the repo, fixed retrieval points at transitions, judgment instead of scores). The effective change (the librarian in the dev-team review) was conceptual and structural, which no tool could have delivered. The server costs restarts, stale code in running sessions, and the mcp/chromadb dependencies, whereas the file path needs only the stdlib.

Earlier plan: a 2026-10-04 audit plan had the plugin keep .mcp.json with a venv bootstrap and mcp__plugin_ai-mem_ai-mem__* tool names. The todo_plugin_packaging todo says this is superseded: the file path is stdlib-only, so the plugin needs only python3 and no venv.

Supporting facts: the 2026-10-04 file backend decision removed Chroma as the store, and the record files became the only store (the MCP server still exists in the code at this point). The mem CLI (add, link, delete, context, lint/doctor stubs) was merged in c5f630e per learning_dev_team_plugin_step2_done_2026_10_10, so the CLI half is being built. The 2026-09-29 learning records a practical cost of the server: after a persistence-layer change, old server processes kept running old code and the client kept a cached tool schema.

Perspective: the records carry no perspective key. The decision is recorded as ai-mem's own domain decision; no dissent from another role is recorded. Not covered: the docs/target_picture_plugin.md briefing and docs/handoff-2026-10-10.md are outside my read scope, so I did not read them. I found no record on a CLI-only alternative being rejected in favor of keeping the MCP server.
